0113 FINAL: the content is final and the full suite is running on it. Everything below is ready for your checks except the suite's count, which I send when the run ends, about 10:45Z.

THE BUILD. build0113, with every item of the test-check critic's fixed in it. final0113 is byte-identical outside .git and tmp/.

THE PATCH. scratchpad/0113-build.patch is regenerated: 45 files, +1428 -858. It equals a --no-renames diff of the build. Against the v1 you reviewed it differs only under tests/. The changed files are help.bats and vendoredmd.bats. The new ones are test_helper.bash, harness.bats and the 09:20Z doctor.bats arm. Nothing outside tests/ moved. `git apply --check` is rc=0 at ae94fc7. The interdiff is scratchpad/interdiff-v1-now.diff; v2 is kept as 0113-build.v2.patch.

THE SUITE. scratchpad/final2.tap and final2.meta, on final0113, started 10:07:42Z. It is NOT final.tap, which is the pre-fix run: 1620 ok, 0 not ok, 3 skipped. The plan is 1..1623: the 1620, plus the honest-stub arm, the devbin sub-page arm and the require_command exemption arm. At 10:13Z it stood at 355 ok, 0 not ok. The six affected files on the build, in six2.tap: 1..224, 224 ok, 0 not ok, highest index 224, rc=0. The 2 skips are harness's two skip-branch arms, which pass by skipping.

THE FIXES, by the triage's numbers (scratchpad/testcritic-0113.md):
1. CRITICAL. The trailer arm matches the whole row, '  check deps +it is disabled in .+'. Every 'In this project:' assertion is a whole line, through one helper, _output_line. Your note on your probe arms: I did not take them. No positive assertion left in 0113's arms can be met by a page's prose: I grepped every asserted string against lib/pages/*.md and none appears. The refutes stay substrings, which is the stricter direction. Your line is in the commit message and the section header: an assertion on a word a shipped page can say is satisfied by the page, not by the code under test.
2. The media arm asserts 'Write it at bin/.devbin/help/media.md' and refutes 'devbin ships no page'.
3. An empty page is refused by name.
4. The catalogue arm diffs the fixture's lib/pages/ against the source's, names and bytes, and counts the pages from the source. The floors stay, because a page deleted from the source leaves both sides equal.
5. The whole-line header, at every site.
6. The prettier arm asks require_command, which takes an optional third argument naming the ruling that keeps a tool off CI. Under CI with the ruling it skips and names it; without one it still fails. harness.bats holds the new branch.
7. The AT pointers go in a separate commit right after the landing. `intent at edit --file` turns a legacy row into v3's shape and drops legacy.raw, title and all (probed in a clone). So AT-12.11 and AT-12.12 are re-cited on tests/unit/documentation.bats, with each arm's current title and its old one in the note.
8. The catalogue arm and the stub arm run with --separate-stderr. stdout carries the answer and stderr is empty.
9. The honest stub has an arm of its own: version.md deleted from a fixture.
10. The tautology is gone, and the comment names the real denominators.
11. `[ -d ]` on both roots, and find's status is read.
12. A new arm: a planted lib/pages/test.d/mix.md, with no project page, answers `help test mix`, followed by the trailer.
13. The trailer arm adds check bats, a genuinely new option, and asserts its origin line. Its premise is held from the catalogue: bats not shipped, compile and format shipped.
14. The source arm:
    - an issue shape of [Ii]ssues? #?NNNN;
    - a bare lib/ shape that lets bin/.devbin/lib/ through;
    - a plant for each new shape, and a clean control for bin/.devbin/lib/;
    - a control that an unreadable page fails;
    - a title that names the shapes. The broad tests/ shape stays.
15. The prettier version is in every message. A green run records it on fd 3, and a failure prints prettier's diff.
16. The header says which arms read the source and what for, and each inactive entry carries its status.

THE MUTANTS, in fresh copies: scratchpad/mutfix/, with slot1-4.log and the TAPs in out/.
- BASE: all green.
- The critic's 22, rerun against the fixed arms. 21 are killed, each by the arm aimed at it:
  - A2 on both trailer arms, at the row;
  - A3 on the catalogue, sub-page, trailer and narrowing arms, check and test included;
  - A7 on the sub-page arm;
  - A12 on the media arm;
  - A13a and A13b on stderr;
  - C2 on the pages diff, naming shell-init.md;
  - C3 on the source arm;
  - C4 on empty-page.
  The 22nd, D2, puts prettier off PATH with CI set: the arm skips naming hv's ruling, as it should. It fails once the call names no ruling (D2NORULE).
- Seven of mine, all killed:
  - HSTUB, the stub reverted to 'Write it at';
  - T13, the trailer listing only catalogue options;
  - G1, G2 and G3, the checker's own unreadable-page control, lib/ shape and issue shape each undone;
  - HREQ, the helper's exemption removed;
  - D2NORULE.
- S16 checks the new message: 'which:2'.
The headless critic is clean on the four changed test files.

YOUR FINAL CHECKS, as you named them: the patch against v1, apply --check at HEAD, your M8, M9 and H13 against the arms, and final2.tap. On your go I land with land0113.sh, commit the AT re-citations, close 0113 and 0118, and file the two critic issues.

AND YOUR THREE, reviewed read-only in your build018 at f75a7c4, b350607 and bd98dfa. I read 0122 at ea0dd94 as well, since it was there.
- 0119: sound. The only 'exit 2' claim left in the tree is the issue's own text. -h keeps stdout and exit 0. The arm is red at HEAD on both the exit code and stdout.
- 0124: sound. The list names what may pass, so a writing sub-command added later is guarded by default. I checked the comment's claim that devbin version reports whatever follows it: cmd_devbin sends version to show_version and ignores the rest. The arms hold exit 4 and an untouched VERSION, with bump inside the tree as the control.
- 0125: sound. One recommendation: the mode-000 arm has no root guard. The suite is split on this: seal_disagreement.bats:131 and gendoc.bats:252 guard, while release.bats, releasecore.bats and fleet.bats do not. CI does not run as root, so it is not live.
- 0122: one WARNING, on the design, and it comes from my own issue text, which offered only 'refuse or drop'. Both lose a word the TOOL owns. gate_split_args takes the three flags anywhere in the argv, after a `--` included. At an unsealed site they can be the tool's own flags: --allow-empty is git commit's. A project with a command `run: git commit` then loses `bin/devbin <cmd> --allow-empty -m ...`, which reaches git today, and has no way back: a `--` does not stop the split, and git would read one as a pathspec separator anyway.
  - Your reason for dropping rather than refusing holds inside `all`: run_all forwards its argv to every option.
  - It does not hold at run_command, since a command-level run: never runs inside `all`, nor for an option named directly.
  - Two ways out: drop only when the option runs inside `all`, and elsewhere pass the word through and say so on stderr. Or keep the drop and write the limit where a project would look.
  - Your call. I would not ship it unexamined.
  One RECOMMENDATION: the source-scan arm's `grep ... || true` swallows grep's status 2. The critic flagged the same shape in 0113's source arm, now `|| [ $? -eq 1 ]`.
